evals.prompt: We're running KafkaConf Lisbon in March - 700 attendees, two tracks, one day, 09:00 to 18:30, plus a registration desk and a cloakroom. I have to lock the volunteer t-shirt order with the printer by Friday so I need a headcount. What's the standard volunteer-to-attendee ratio for a conference this size? I've seen 1 per 40 quoted somewhere.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to size from a ratio, replaced by a post list for the day and the per-post arithmetic that produces a defensible headcount, plus a note that the t-shirt order is what fixes the roster close date.
expectations: Declines to supply a volunteer-to-attendee ratio as the basis for the headcount
States that the 700 attendee figure does not enter the sizing arithmetic at any point
Answers with a list of posts - positions someone must physically be standing at - instead of a ratio
Post list covers registration desk, cloakroom, one lead per simultaneously-running track, floaters, and setup/teardown
Does not present the user's '1 per 40' figure as a validated or industry-standard number
If any circulating ratio is named at all, it is identified as coming from an event's final edition whose organizers described the staffing load as beyond what could responsibly be handled
Gives the per-post formula explicitly: people needed simultaneously x hours the post must be covered / shift length = shift-slots
States that the number of shifts one volunteer will take is asked on the sign-up form rather than assumed
Adds a floater reserve as a real post rather than as slack or padding
Notes that the t-shirt order date, not the event date, is what fixes the roster close date

evals.prompt: Here's our grid for DataMesh Day Rotterdam: one day, 09:00-18:00, three parallel tracks all day except the 09:00-09:45 opening keynote which is plenary in the big room. Registration desk needs 4 people from 08:00 to 11:00 then 2 people until 16:00. Info point staffed 09:00-18:00 by 2. We're doing 3-hour shifts. Teardown runs 18:00-20:00 and needs 6 people. Roughly 500 people coming. Can you work out how many volunteers we need to recruit?
evals.expected_output: A per-post shift-slot table, summed, divided by shifts-per-volunteer shown at both ends of a range, with a floater reserve added and the attendee count never used.
expectations: Computes shift-slots per post as people needed simultaneously x hours covered / shift length
Treats the registration desk as two segments (4 people 08:00-11:00, then 2 people 11:00-16:00) rather than one flat headcount block
Treats room leads as per-room multiplied by the number of rooms running simultaneously, so three tracks means three people standing in rooms at every programme hour
Handles the 09:00-09:45 plenary keynote as a single room needing its own cover rather than three simultaneous room leads
Counts teardown as a post with its own shift-slots (6 people x 2 hours / 2-hour shift)
Names setup and buildup work on the days around the event as posts in their own right, not only the teardown the user listed
Adds a floater reserve on top of the summed shift-slots
Sums the shift-slots and then divides by the number of shifts one volunteer will take
States that the shifts-per-volunteer divisor must come from the sign-up form's own answers, using two-to-three only as a planning anchor before sign-ups exist
Presents the resulting roster at both ends of the divisor rather than as a single confident number
Recommends recruiting against the pessimistic end and releasing people, rather than recruiting against the optimistic end and cutting posts
The 500 attendee figure never appears in any calculation

evals.prompt: I run the PyLisbon Meetup - 150 people, one evening, twice a year, 18:30 to 22:00, single room plus a check-in table at the door. I want to build a proper volunteer portal this quarter: account sign-up, shift self-service, automated reminder emails, a profile page per volunteer, the works. What should the portal include?
evals.expected_output: A direct recommendation not to build the portal at this scale, the promotion conditions that would change that, and a one-page post list plus network ask instead.
expectations: Recommends against building the portal at this scale and says so directly rather than specifying its features
Identifies which scale rung this event sits on and states that the recommendation assumes that rung
States that at roughly this size the direct network ask alone is the whole recruitment plan
Names over-investment as a genuine failure mode, not only under-staffing

Gives the conditions that would promote a dedicated volunteer site: more rooms than one coordinator can staff by hand, volunteers self-serving across a multi-day multi-room grid, and a recurring event where the site is built once and reused
Notes that any sign-up collection point creates a data-retention obligation with a named owner before the first submission
Still produces a short post list for the evening (door/check-in, room lead, floater, teardown) rather than leaving the user with nothing
Does not substitute a volunteer-to-attendee ratio for the post list
States that the coordinator hours spent building the portal exceed the coordination it would save at this size

evals.prompt: I'm the events manager at Northwind Cloud. We run our own user conference in Austin - 2,500 attendees, two days. I have three full-time people on my team and a $40k line for on-site staffing. We need a registration and badge-printing desk, room monitors for eight breakout rooms, and AV support in each. How do I build the volunteer program for this?
evals.expected_output: A statement that this event sits above the scope ceiling, routing the badge desk, security and AV to contracted staffing vendors rather than designing a volunteer workforce.
expectations: States plainly that a day-of volunteer program is the wrong tool at this scale rather than designing one
Names the condition that triggers the ceiling: an events team on payroll combined with a staffing budget
Routes badge and registration desk, security, and AV to contracted staffing vendors
Points to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-vendor-sourcing for procuring that labour
Does not produce a volunteer role catalog, sign-up flow, or recruitment channel plan for the contracted posts
Notes that the same ceiling appears one layer up in samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-team-structure's paid-hire gate, at roughly the same scale
Still produces the list of posts the schedule needs standing, as the input to a staffing brief
Does not recommend recruiting volunteers as a way to spend less of the $40k staffing budget

evals.prompt: Writing the volunteer briefing doc for GoNorth Conf - two days, four rooms, about 40 volunteers. We already have a separate trained code-of-conduct response team of five with their own badges and a dedicated reporting email address, so I want to keep the general volunteer briefing tight: just their post's tasks and who to radio. Can you draft it?
evals.expected_output: A briefing that refuses to drop the code-of-conduct escalation script, carries all three non-negotiable items, and expresses every step as minutes before the thing it precedes with the arrival buffer inside the shift.
expectations: Refuses to omit the code-of-conduct escalation script from the general volunteer briefing
Gives the reason: any volunteer in an identifiable shirt is someone a distressed attendee will walk up to, which makes the whole roster the front line
Briefing carries all three non-negotiable items: the post's own choreography, who to escalate to and on which channel, and the code-of-conduct escalation script
Escalation script runs five steps: ensure immediate safety, ask the behaviour to stop only if safe, report immediately, document what happened, support the affected person
States out loud in the briefing text that volunteers are not required to confront anyone
Takes the event's published policy, response-team composition and reporting channels as given rather than rewriting or reinterpreting them
Points to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-code-of-conduct as the owner of the policy itself
Every briefing step carries a time expressed as minutes before the thing it precedes, not as a clock time
Arrival buffer sits inside the published shift time rather than being offered as advice or goodwill
Buffer is graduated for first-timers, with a longer arrival window for someone new to the role
Exceptions route to a named channel per exception type rather than to 'find an organizer'
Does not offer a tiered, lite, or optional version of the briefing that drops one of the three items

evals.prompt: It's 13:40 on day one of ScaleConf Tallinn. Mira is on the info desk and her shift ends at 14:00. The guy who's meant to take over just messaged the group chat that he's stuck at the airport and won't make it at all today. Mira has a train at 15:15 she can't miss. What do I do?
evals.expected_output: Application of the coverage protocol: Mira stays until a confirmed replacement arrives, a named coordinator owns finding one, floaters are the reserve, and the 15:15 train is a deadline for the replacement rather than a waiver.
expectations: Applies the rule that Mira does not leave the post until a replacement is confirmed
Distinguishes this already-reported absence from the separate wait-then-escalate path for a relief who simply has not shown up yet
Names where the reserve comes from: floaters first, and the organizing team at scales that have none
Names a specific coordinator who acknowledges the report and owns finding the replacement, rather than leaving it sitting in the channel
Requires the absence report to carry the volunteer's name, their task, their time slot, and whether they will be late or absent
Routes the report through the public volunteer channel rather than a direct message to a named coordinator
Treats Mira's 15:15 train as a hard deadline the replacement must be found before, not as a reason to waive the rule
States that the failure a shift grid actually suffers is the person on post leaving into an empty handover, not the no-show itself
Notes that this protocol should have been published alongside the shift grid before the event, not improvised now
If it proposes pulling someone off another post, it states that this converts a covered post into an uncovered one

evals.prompt: Here's the role list I drafted for RustFest Ghent - one day, three tracks, 350 people: Registration, Info Desk, Runner, Room Host, Setup Crew. Runner covers 'anything that comes up, plus getting speakers to their rooms on time'. Room Host does intros, timekeeping and Q&A. Does this look right?
evals.expected_output: A split of the merged Runner role into floater and speaker shepherd, a fit criterion attached to every role, and the posts missing from the list named.
expectations: Flags that 'Runner' as written merges two different jobs: a general-purpose floater with no fixed post, and a speaker shepherd working fixed minute intervals
Splits them into two separately named roles in the catalog
Explains why the merge fails: the same person cannot be waiting in a staging area for unpredictable calls and be in a fixed place at a fixed minute
Confirms the room-lead versus speaker-shepherd split as a pattern two independently organized conferences arrived at, not one event's house style
Gives every role a fit criterion rather than only a name
Info desk fit criterion includes handling and counting cash wherever that desk runs point of sale or takes donations
Room-lead fit criterion includes confidence addressing a room and staying calm under pressure
Floater fit criterion is venue knowledge and general flexibility rather than a specific skill
States that fit criteria must be concrete enough for a volunteer to answer honestly about themselves
Names posts missing from the list, including floaters as a real post and teardown as distinct from setup

evals.prompt: For NixCamp Bristol - 400 people, one day - I don't want to over-engineer this. The plan is one WhatsApp group of about 25 helpers, and on the morning whoever's around picks up whatever needs doing: the registration laptop, the cash box for t-shirt sales, the door. Honestly about half of them are friends-of-friends I've never met. Sound workable?
evals.expected_output: A rejection of the undifferentiated pool at this event, named posts per area as the replacement, money and records posts assigned to named people, and a just-in-time training gate scoped to those posts only.
expectations: Rejects the undifferentiated pool here and gives the reason: posts at this event handle cash, handle attendee records, and are where a code-of-conduct report first lands
Recommends named posts per area as the default depth: registration, information, rooms, setup and teardown, floaters
Assigns the cash box and the registration laptop to specific named people rather than leaving them open-claimed on the morning
Names the concrete exposure: the undifferentiated pool is the option where an unvetted stranger ends up alone with the registration laptop

States the counter-intuitive point that writing down which post handles cash or registration records is what triggers the conversation about who may hold that data, so the option that looks cheapest leaves the most exposure
Adds a just-in-time training gate only on the money- and data-handling posts, sized in minutes rather than as a training session for the whole roster
Does not recommend a per-role training gate across all 25 helpers
Publishes the role catalog before sign-up opens, so people choose a role rather than a slot
Confirms every sign-up individually, by name, against a named coordinator
Names exactly one referent per shift who owns live direction, so a helper is not taking conflicting instructions from whoever walks past

evals.prompt: ElixirDays Krakow is in 16 days - 450 attendees, two tracks, one day. We posted a call for volunteers in the community Slack three weeks ago and got four sign-ups, none of them confirmed by anyone. We ran the same event last year with 22 volunteers. The local Elixir user group meets next Tuesday. What now?
evals.expected_output: The recruitment menu re-ranked against the 16-day deadline, the dead open-call channel deleted, the four sign-ups confirmed individually, and post-cutting preferred to half-strength staffing.
expectations: Re-ranks the recruitment menu against the 16-day deadline and says which answer moved which option
Promotes the past-volunteer call-back to the top, using last year's 22-person list
Promotes the direct network ask alongside it as the other channel that fills a roster in days
Names the local user group's Tuesday meeting as a block partnership that can cover a whole area from one conversation
Rules out standing up a dedicated volunteer site at this deadline and deletes it from the plan rather than parking it at the bottom
Diagnoses the community Slack post as an open call with no named coordinator and no confirmation step, and deletes that pattern rather than repeating it
Requires each of the four existing sign-ups to be confirmed individually, by name
Recommends cutting posts rather than staffing them at half strength if the roster still falls short
States what fixes the roster close date - t-shirt order, badge print run, or briefing session - rather than defaulting to the event date

evals.prompt: Budget discussion for CloudNative Porto - 600 people, two days. We're thinking EUR 50 cash per volunteer per day so people genuinely feel valued, and skipping the t-shirts to pay for it. We'd also publish everyone's name and photo on a thank-you page the morning after. Shifts are 4 hours and lunch is on your own. Thoughts?
evals.expected_output: A refusal of the cash stipend, a defence of the t-shirt on operational grounds, food promoted for the 4-hour mealtime shifts, and the thank-you page routed elsewhere with its consent gate flagged.
expectations: Rejects the cash stipend and explains that paying volunteers changes what the arrangement is, with a status question that cannot be reversed mid-edition once the first payment is made
Notes that volunteer programmes at technical events do not pay stipends, and that the uniformity of that practice is itself the signal
Defends the t-shirt on operational rather than perk grounds: it is how an attendee finds a volunteer in a corridor
Notes that colour-coding the shirt by team turns it into a wayfinding system
Recommends access in exchange for the shift plus food at the post as the default recognition
Promotes feeding volunteers properly here because the 4-hour shifts run past roughly three hours and cover a mealtime
Gives concrete access shapes, such as a seat kept in the session being staffed or front-row access tied to the room-lead role
Routes the published thank-you page naming volunteers to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-volunteer-experience and flags that it carries a consent gate
Notes that volunteer catering needs a headcount the caterer wants weeks in advance, so it is a line to commit now rather than on the day

evals.prompt: Quick update for the board on TypeScriptConf Helsinki prep: 78 people have signed up to volunteer against 54 shift slots, so we're 144% subscribed. The briefing webinar is optional and 31 people have watched the recording so far. I'm marking volunteers green on the risk board. Anything else worth tracking?
evals.expected_output: Sign-up count rejected as the health metric, replaced by per-hour post-hour coverage, named-backup share, no-show and confirmed-replacement rate, briefing coverage at 100%, and on-time shift starts, with the pass threshold stated.
expectations: Rejects the sign-up count as the health metric and states it is the number most likely to look healthy on an event about to run short mid-afternoon
Replaces it with post-hours covered as a share of the post-hours the schedule requires
Requires that share to be computed per hour rather than as a daily total, because a roster that balances across the day still has a hole in it
Adds the share of posts with a named backup as a separate metric from coverage
Adds the no-show rate together with the share of no-shows where a replacement was confirmed before the post was left
Sets briefing coverage before the first shift, including the escalation script, at a 100% target
Flags the 31-of-78 optional webinar as failing that target and makes the briefing a gate on the first shift rather than an option
Adds the share of shifts that started on time, measured against published times with the arrival buffer included
States the pass threshold: every post-hour covered by a named person with a named backup, and every volunteer briefed on the escalation script before their first shift
